files.name: m_axil_regfile_dec.sv
m_axil_regfile.sv

open_points: Section 4 / REQ-PAR-003 (RF-4-06, SHOULD): RR-11 does not allow system tasks, so the parameter range check uses an elaboration-time $error inside `ifndef SYNTHESIS`. I read REQ-PAR-003 as the specification asking for this behaviour. Yosys defines SYNTHESIS, so synthesis skips the check. Verilator lint and simulation still run it.

Section 5 / REQ-PAR-002: LPARA_REGS_W is a localparam in the module body, equal to PARA_NUM_REGS*32. The o_regs port width is written as PARA_NUM_REGS*32 rather than LPARA_REGS_W, because tools differ on accepting a localparam in the ANSI parameter port list. The width is the same; o_regs is driven from an internal vector declared with LPARA_REGS_W.

Sections 7.4 / 7.5 (REQ-WR-027, REQ-RD-014): outside reset, o_s_axi_bresp, o_s_axi_rdata and o_s_axi_rresp keep the value of the last response while their valid is 0. They are reset to 0 (OKAY / 0x0) as REQ-RST-002 requires.

Section 13 (REQ-IMP-004): I chose to reset the held write-transaction payload (decoded address, wdata, wstrb) asynchronously to 0, because it counts as 'transaction state'. This is the cautious choice, although a valid bit already qualifies these values.

Section 1.3 / 7.1: i_s_axi_awprot, i_s_axi_arprot and address bits [1:0] are unused, as the spec requires. The Verilator UNUSEDSIGNAL warning is waived with a `// WAIVER:` comment on a single XOR-reduced sink signal named `unused_inputs`.

Section 7.1 (decode): a write's decoded result (register hit, mapped flag, 4-bit register number) is stored at the AW transfer instead of the full address. This keeps storage small (section 13 storage guidance), and the behaviour is the same as decoding the stored address at Ec.

Section 7.3 (REQ-WR-017 / REQ-ERR-004): a write with wstrb = 4'b0000 is handled like any other write. It completes at Ec with the normal bvalid timing and the normal response, and no byte lane is enabled, so no register bit changes.
notes:
I've written the RTL in two files, listed leaf first. Nothing has been compiled or simulated, so the Verilator lint and Yosys checks the rules require have not been run.

- `m_axil_regfile_dec.sv` is a combinational address decoder. It compares every bit of the word index (address bits [PARA_ADDR_W-1:2]), so there is no aliasing. It flags register k when 0 <= k < PARA_NUM_REGS, and the status register at word index 16; every other address is unmapped. The top module uses one copy for writes and one for reads.
- `m_axil_regfile.sv` is the top module, with the parameters and ports of INTERFACE.md.

Write path:
- The write address and write data are taken separately, in either order or at the same edge. Flags record when each is held until the B transfer.
- awready and wready are registered as the inverse of the next cycle's held state. They are 0 during reset and in the cycle that ends at R1, 1 from R1, and 1 again in the cycle that starts at Eb.
- The edge Ec is when both have been taken and at least one was taken at that edge. At Ec the byte lanes enabled by wstrb are written into register k, bvalid goes to 1 and bresp is set (OKAY for a register or the status register, SLVERR for an unmapped address).
- Full write throughput is one write every 2 cycles.

Read path:
- At the AR transfer the block captures the register value, i_status for 0x40, or 0 with SLVERR for an unmapped address. A write completing at the same edge therefore returns the old value.
- rvalid goes to 1, and arready is 0 until the cycle that starts at the R transfer. Full read throughput is one read every 2 cycles.
- The read path does not depend on the write channels, apart from the register values it returns.

All flip-flops reset asynchronously on i_rst_n, which also clears any pending address, data or response. Every output comes straight from a flip-flop.
